bootstrap_mode.label: Bootstrap Mode
bootstrap_mode.question: How much setup guidance should AI Ops use before applying project files?

options.label: Fast Track
options.description: Use a short question flow and minimal safe defaults.
options.changes: Creates a lighter .ai_project shape and leaves advanced choices deferred.
options.recommended_when: New users, small projects, idea discovery, or solo work.
options.risk: Some team, branch, and workflow details may need expansion later.

options.label: Guided Full
options.description: Compare team, role, workflow, ownership, board, and branch options step by step.
options.changes: Creates the fuller .ai_project shape with detailed operating decisions.
options.recommended_when: Code projects, multiple agents, PR flows, or multi-team setup.

options.label: Manual
options.description: Use custom project decisions without the standard guided flow.
options.changes: Requires the operator to keep required fields coherent.
options.recommended_when: Existing organizations with their own process.
options.risk: Higher chance of missing required AI Ops fields.

options.label: Migrated
options.description: Mark a project that was created or upgraded through migration.
options.changes: Preserves existing project decisions and records migration provenance.
options.recommended_when: Existing .ai_project setups upgraded from an older AI Ops version.
options.risk: May need migration validation before strict operation.

start_context.label: Start Context
start_context.question: What kind of project start is this?

options.label: New project with requirement
options.description: A new project or business starts from an idea, requirement, or rough plan.
options.changes: Readiness is checked before implementation roles are activated.
options.recommended_when: The user knows what they want to build at least roughly.

options.label: Assigned or existing project
options.description: AI Ops is being applied to an existing repository, task, or handoff.
options.changes: Project scan and source-of-truth verification come first.
options.recommended_when: There is existing code, documentation, or company work to take over.

options.label: Blank slate discovery
options.description: The user does not know what to build yet and wants to explore from zero.
options.changes: No product task is created until Direction work produces a candidate direction.
options.recommended_when: Idea discovery, research, or problem finding.

options.label: Rescue or recovery
options.description: The project needs stabilization before normal planning or implementation.
options.changes: Build, test, missing context, and broken process checks are prioritized.
options.recommended_when: Broken builds, missing documentation, abandoned work, or failed handoff.

options.label: Migration or modernization
options.description: The main goal is to move or modernize an existing system.
options.changes: Scope, compatibility, rollback, and verification gates become primary.
options.recommended_when: Framework upgrades, architecture migration, repo restructuring.

options.label: Ops setup only
options.description: The user only wants AI Ops operating files, not product work.
options.changes: Creates operating setup and defers product tasks.
options.recommended_when: Installing AI Ops into a project before actual work starts.

options.label: Scale up existing ops
options.description: An existing AI Ops setup needs more teams, roles, or stricter workflow.
options.changes: Current .ai_project decisions are reviewed before expansion.
options.recommended_when: A solo or small setup is growing into team operation.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The start context does not fit the standard options.
options.changes: The user must record a custom summary and required decisions.
options.recommended_when: Special operating environments or mixed project contexts.

readiness_level.label: Readiness Level
readiness_level.question: How ready is the project for execution?

options.label: Idea only
options.description: The idea is still vague or only stated in a sentence.
options.changes: Implementation is deferred and Direction work comes first.
options.recommended_when: The user needs to clarify problem, audience, and value.

options.label: Idea structured
options.description: The goal and core features are roughly understood.
options.changes: Product direction and MVP scope can be drafted before execution.
options.recommended_when: The user can describe what the product should do.

options.label: Planning ready
options.description: Planning exists, but implementation breakdown is not ready.
options.changes: Task breakdown, source of truth, and verification criteria are prepared.
options.recommended_when: Requirements exist but work items and tests are not clear.

options.label: Implementation ready
options.description: Requirements and acceptance criteria are ready enough to build.
options.changes: Execution and Verification roles can be activated.
options.recommended_when: The first approved task can be created safely.

options.label: Existing project scan required
options.description: Existing files must be scanned before decisions are trusted.
options.changes: Source-of-truth and code/document consistency are checked first.
options.recommended_when: AI Ops is being applied to an existing repo.

options.label: Discovery required
options.description: The problem, user, or value is not clear enough yet.
options.changes: Discovery tasks and Direction questions come before build tasks.
options.recommended_when: The user is exploring possibilities.

options.label: Recovery required
options.description: The project must be stabilized before normal execution.
options.changes: Recovery tasks and verification criteria take priority.
options.recommended_when: Build, test, dependency, or documentation state is unreliable.

options.label: Ops only
options.description: Only the AI Ops operating setup is needed now.
options.changes: Product direction and implementation tasks remain unresolved.
options.recommended_when: The project is only installing or reviewing the harness.

operating_mode.label: Operating Mode
operating_mode.question: How much operating structure does this project need?

options.label: Solo Light
options.description: One person or one session can hold multiple roles with minimal ceremony.
options.changes: Uses a single board and a shorter workflow for simple tasks.
options.recommended_when: Small projects, idea work, or first-time AI Ops use.

options.label: Team Basic
options.description: Lead, Execution, and Verification responsibilities are separated.
options.changes: Task setup, implementation, and verification become distinct handoffs.
options.recommended_when: A project needs safer work separation without full PR process.

options.label: Team PR
options.description: Team Basic plus task branch, PR, review, and merge ownership.
options.changes: Branch and PR policy becomes part of task execution.
options.recommended_when: Code projects where change history and merge control matter.

options.label: Multi Team
options.description: Multiple teams own separate paths, domains, platforms, or modules.
options.changes: Team ownership, team boards, and coordination policy become required.
options.recommended_when: iOS, Android, Web, Backend, or domain teams work in parallel.
options.risk: Requires stronger ownership and dependency records.

options.label: Enterprise
options.description: Division, QA, Release, and broader governance are included.
options.changes: More approval gates and operating documents are expected.
options.recommended_when: Long-lived products, multiple divisions, or release governance.

team_pattern.label: Team Pattern
team_pattern.question: How should team ownership be divided?

options.label: Single team
options.description: One team owns most project work.
options.changes: Uses one project board and one shared operating model.
options.recommended_when: Early projects, solo work, or unclear team boundaries.

options.label: Functional teams
options.description: Teams are divided by function such as product, development, QA, or release.
options.changes: Role and handoff boundaries become more explicit.
options.recommended_when: Specialized responsibilities matter more than code paths.

options.label: Platform teams
options.description: Teams are divided by platform such as iOS, Android, Web, or Backend.
options.changes: Path ownership and verification criteria are configured per platform.
options.recommended_when: Multiple platform codebases are developed in parallel.

options.label: Cross-functional
options.description: A team owns end-to-end product slices across disciplines.
options.changes: Domain ownership can matter more than directory ownership.
options.recommended_when: Feature teams deliver across product, design, backend, and frontend.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The user defines team names and ownership rules directly.
options.changes: Requires explicit role, path, domain, source-of-truth, and board decisions.
options.recommended_when: The project already has a custom organization shape.

workflow_policy.label: Workflow Policy
workflow_policy.question: How strict should task state flow be?

options.label: Standard vNext
options.description: Use the full proposed-to-done flow with approval, execution, verification, and completion review.
options.changes: Clearer accountability with more state transitions.
options.recommended_when: Most development projects.

options.label: Skip scoped for simple tasks
options.description: Simple tasks may move from proposed to approved without a separate scoped state.
options.changes: Reduces overhead for small changes.
options.recommended_when: Solo Light, documentation cleanup, or low-risk changes.
options.risk: Ambiguous ownership should still use the standard flow.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The project defines its own state flow and transition rules.
options.changes: Requires explicit state, role, and approval mapping.
options.recommended_when: An existing issue or PR workflow must be preserved.

ownership_model.label: Ownership Model
ownership_model.question: How should responsibility for changes be decided?

options.label: Path only
options.description: Ownership is determined by file and directory paths.
options.changes: Easy to understand but weak for cross-cutting features.
options.recommended_when: Small projects with clear code boundaries.

options.label: Path plus domain
options.description: Ownership uses both paths and product or technical domains.
options.changes: Cross-path features can still have a clear owner.
options.recommended_when: Most app and service projects.

options.label: Document ownership
options.description: Source-of-truth documents have explicit owners.
options.changes: Requirements, architecture, and API docs are protected as decision sources.
options.recommended_when: Planning, design, or architecture documents drive execution.

options.label: Strict parallel control
options.description: Parallel work is restricted when ownership or path conflicts may occur.
options.changes: Reduces merge and rework risk at the cost of speed.
options.recommended_when: Migration, multi-team work, or sensitive code areas.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The project defines its own ownership rules.
options.changes: Requires clear conflict resolution and approval policy.
options.recommended_when: Existing CODEOWNERS or company ownership policy must be kept.

coordination.label: Coordination Policy
coordination.question: How should parallel work be coordinated?

options.label: Single active task
options.description: Only one core task is active at a time.
options.changes: Minimizes conflict and is easy for new users.
options.recommended_when: Solo Light, early projects, or high uncertainty.

options.label: Parallel with locks
options.description: Parallel tasks are allowed when locks and ownership do not conflict.
options.changes: Requires task lock metadata and dependency checks.
options.recommended_when: Multiple agents work on separate areas.

options.label: Team board coordination
options.description: Team boards and the project board coordinate parallel work.
options.changes: Team-level status and cross-team dependencies must be maintained.
options.recommended_when: Multi-team or platform-team operation.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The project defines its own coordination rules.
options.changes: Requires explicit blocked, dependency, and conflict handling.
options.recommended_when: An existing PM or issue process must be preserved.

board_model.label: Board Model
board_model.question: Where should work status be tracked?

options.label: Project board only
options.description: Use one .ai_project/task_board.md for the whole project.
options.changes: Simplest board structure.
options.recommended_when: Single team, early projects, or Solo Light.

options.label: Project plus team board
options.description: Use one project board plus team-level boards.
options.changes: Separates overall priority from team execution state.
options.recommended_when: Multi-team or platform-team operation.

options.label: Custom views
options.description: Use custom views by role, team, domain, release, or product line.
options.changes: Flexible but adds maintenance overhead.
options.recommended_when: Enterprise or complex reporting needs.

branch_pr.label: Branch / PR Policy
branch_pr.question: How should Git branch, PR, and merge control work?

options.label: Pending decision
options.description: No branch or PR strategy is selected yet.
options.changes: Git initialization, branch creation, PR, and merge remain deferred.
options.recommended_when: The target is not a Git repo or implementation is not ready.

options.label: Simple safe
options.description: Use conservative Git behavior with explicit user approval for risky actions.
options.changes: Keeps main protected and requires approval before push or merge.
options.recommended_when: Small code projects that need safety without heavy process.

options.label: Branch per task
options.description: Each task gets a task branch and can be reviewed before merge.
options.changes: Execution owns task commits; Lead owns merge decision.
options.recommended_when: Most AI-assisted code projects.

options.label: PR required
options.description: Changes must go through PR and independent review.
options.changes: Verification review becomes part of normal completion.
options.recommended_when: Collaborative repositories or protected main branches.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The project defines its own Git strategy.
options.changes: Requires explicit branch, commit, push, review, and merge rules.
options.recommended_when: Existing GitFlow, company policy, or release branch process.

knowledge_mode.label: Knowledge Mode
knowledge_mode.question: How should AI-readable project knowledge be organized?

options.label: Minimal
options.description: Keep only a small AI knowledge index and project brief.
options.changes: Fastest setup and lowest documentation overhead.
options.recommended_when: New users, small projects, or early discovery.

options.label: Indexed
options.description: Maintain an index of important project knowledge and source references.
options.changes: Agents can find relevant context without reading every document.
options.recommended_when: The project already has several important documents.

options.label: Context packs
options.description: Group task-specific knowledge into small context packs.
options.changes: Better for large projects and specialized role sessions.
options.recommended_when: Long documents or many domains make context loading expensive.

options.label: External source of truth
options.description: Reference external systems for canonical product or engineering knowledge.
options.changes: AI Ops stores pointers and summaries, not the full source content.
options.recommended_when: Docs live in Notion, Jira, Confluence, Figma, or another system.

options.label: Custom
options.description: The project defines its own knowledge structure.
options.changes: Requires explicit update and ownership rules.
options.recommended_when: Existing knowledge management should be preserved.
